text:
APIs, or Application Programming Interfaces, allow different software systems to communicate with each other. When working with an API, your code sends HTTP requests to a server, and the server responds with data, usually in JSON format. This data can then be read and used by your program.

Authentication is often required to access an API. You might need an API key or a token in your request header to prove who you are. It is also important to be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain period. If you exceed them, the server may temporarily block you.

Finally, always handle errors gracefully. Check the response status code and provide helpful messages to users when something goes wrong. Good error handling makes your application more reliable.
